   MCP: every iOS Simulator session shares driver port 22087, so MCP calls can read and tap the wrong Simulator   #3611 New issue Copy link New issue Copy link Open Bug #3647 Open MCP: every iOS Simulator session shares driver port 22087, so MCP calls can read and tap the wrong Simulator #3611 Bug #3647 Copy link Description lofi-coding opened  on Sep 18, 2026 Issue body actions Is there an existing issue for this? 
 
  I have searched the existing issues and didn't find mine. 
 
 Steps to reproduce 
 maestro mcp  drives every iOS Simulator through one fixed XCTest driver endpoint,  127.0.0.1:22087 , and adopts whichever runner already answers there. Two MCP servers on one Mac, each asked about its own Simulator (this is how coding-agent sessions use it: every session starts its own server): 
 
 Boot two iOS 26 Simulators, A and B, and open different apps on them, e.g.  xcrun simctl launch <A> com.apple.Preferences  and  xcrun simctl launch <B> com.apple.MobileAddressBook . 
 Start  maestro mcp  (server 1) and call  inspect_screen  with  device_id: <A> . Server 1 starts a driver for A on  127.0.0.1:22087 . 
 Start a second  maestro mcp  (server 2) and call  inspect_screen  with  device_id: <B> . 
 
 The same code path applies inside one server that is asked about A and then B. 
 Actual results 
 In step 3, server 2 does not start a driver for B.  LocalXCTestInstaller.startXCTestRunner  sees A's runner answer  GET 127.0.0.1:22087/status  ("UI Test runner already running") and uses it, so  inspect_screen  for B returns Simulator A's hierarchy, and taps from  run  on B land on A. The call succeeds, so the result looks valid. We saw this between concurrent agent sessions: one session's  inspect_screen  returned another session's Simulator. The one-server case follows from the same code; we have not run it separately. 
 Where it happens (main @  81391e0 ): 
 
 maestro-cli/src/main/java/maestro/cli/mcp/McpMaestroSessionManager.kt :  createIOSDriver  passes  DEFAULT_XCTEST_PORT = 22087  to both  LocalXCTestInstaller(defaultPort = …)  and  XCTestClient(…)  for every device. 
 maestro-ios-driver/src/main/kotlin/xcuitest/installer/LocalXCTestInstaller.kt :  startXCTestRunner  returns early when the status check succeeds, without checking which Simulator that runner lives in.  uninstall()  only kills the runner of its own device, so another device's runner on the port survives  open() . 
 Before 2.6 the MCP tools called  MaestroSessionManager.newSession(driverHostPort = null, …) , which falls back to the same port. 
 
 The CLI fixed this for  maestro test  in  #3138  (per-session driver port,  --driver-host-port , per-device session tracking). The MCP server was not part of that change:  McpMaestroSessionManager , added two days later in  #3288 , still hard-codes the port. 
 A related problem: MCP sessions are cached per device and never recreated. Once the runner stops (another tool starts the same runner app on that Simulator, the Simulator restarts, and so on),  XCTestDriverClient  latches  transportDead  and every later call for that device fails until the MCP server restarts. 
 Expected results 
 Each device session gets a driver endpoint of its own, as the CLI does since  #3138 : for example, allocate a free port per MCP device session (or honor a  --driver-host-port  option on  maestro mcp ) and pass it to both the installer and the client. Before reusing a runner that already answers, check that it belongs to the requested device (for example, have  /status  or  /deviceInfo  report the Simulator UDID). Recreate a cached session whose driver became unreachable instead of failing every later call. 
 About app 
 Not app-specific: any app on an iOS Simulator, including the stock Settings and Contacts apps. 
 About environment 
 
 Java: OpenJDK 21 (Homebrew  openjdk@21 ) 
 macOS 26, Xcode 26, iOS 26 Simulators 
 arm64 (Apple Silicon) 
 
 Logs 
 
 Logs 
 No error is logged. The adoption shows only as `UI Test runner already running, returning`
(LocalXCTestInstaller) in server 2's session, while `lsof -nP -iTCP:22087 -sTCP:LISTEN` shows
a maestro-driver-iosUITests-Runner process under CoreSimulator/Devices/<A>/.
 
 
 Maestro version 
 2.10.0 (the pre-2.6 path above is 2.5.1) 
 How did you install Maestro? 
 Homebrew 
 Anything else? 
 Our workaround: we run the stock  maestro mcp  behind a small launcher. It sets  -Dhttp.proxyHost ,  -Dhttp.proxyPort  and an empty  -Dhttp.nonProxyHosts , so the MCP JVM's OkHttp clients send driver requests through a local proxy that maps 22087 to a port of that Simulator's own. An  xcodebuild  wrapper earlier on the child's PATH rewrites  TEST_RUNNER_PORT  for  test-without-building -destination id=<udid> . It works on 2.5.1 and 2.10.0, but it depends on implementation details; a fix in the MCP session manager would make it unnecessary.
